title: The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.00332v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Distilling the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) into smaller students is a central challenge for efficient deployment. Current approaches face a fundamental tension: optimizing purely for verifiable task rewards (e.g., via GRPO) leads to reward hacking, where students arrive at correct final answers through flawed intermediate logic, while regularizing with soft divergence penalties against a teacher (e.g., KL-based distillation) dilutes task performance and, critically, allows the student to compensate for severe logical violations at one step with high teacher agreement at others. We argue that this averaging is fundamentally misaligned with the nature of reasoning: a chain-of-thought is only as valid as its weakest link. translated_title: 最薄弱环节：基于最坏情况约束强化学习的LLM推理蒸馏
translated_abstract: 将大型语言模型（LLM）的推理能力蒸馏到更小的学生模型中，是实现高效部署的核心挑战。现有方法面临一个根本性矛盾：纯粹针对可验证的任务奖励进行优化（例如通过GRPO）会导致奖励劫持，即学生模型通过有缺陷的中间逻辑却得出正确的最终答案；而采用相对于教师模型的软散度惩罚进行正则化（例如基于KL散度的蒸馏）则会稀释任务性能，且更关键的是，它允许学生模型在其他步骤上与教师高度一致，从而补偿某一步骤上严重的逻辑违规。我们认为这种平均化的处理方式与推理的本质存在根本性错位：思维链的有效性取决于其最薄弱的环节。基于这一观察，我们将推理蒸馏形式化为一个约束强化学习问题，在满足最坏情况约束的前提下最大化任务奖励……
tldr: 该论文提出将LLM推理蒸馏建模为最坏情况约束的强化学习问题，确保学生模型的思维链在每一步都符合教师模型的逻辑标准，避免“最薄弱环节”式的错误推理被平均化指标掩盖。
en_tdlr: This paper formulates LLM reasoning distillation as a constrained RL problem with worst-case constraints, ensuring the student's chain-of-thought is valid at every step rather than allowing flawed reasoning steps to be masked by high average teacher agreement.
